subject.title: [Telegram] 机器人头像更改后无法同步到 Telegram 客户端

question: Should OpenClaw be allowed to mutate a Telegram bot's public profile photo from assistant-avatar changes, and what explicit consent/source-of-truth model should govern it?
rationale: This crosses from local assistant identity rendering into an external account/profile mutation using Telegram bot-token authority, so automation should not choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Explicit opt-in Telegram action
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned one-shot action or UI control that requires operator intent, validates media, reports failures, and has live Telegram proof.

options.title: Manual Telegram ownership
options.body: Keep OpenClaw assistant avatars local and document that Telegram bot profile photos are managed through Telegram/BotFather.

options.title: Automatic bidirectional sync
options.body: Automatically propagate avatar changes between OpenClaw and Telegram, accepting higher surprise, conflict, and privacy risk.

recommendation.title: Explicit opt-in Telegram action
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-owned one-shot action or UI control that requires operator intent, validates media, reports failures, and has live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans assistant identity UX, Telegram channel behavior, and the external-mutation security boundary, and steipete has the strongest merged history on the avatar identity surface.
